issues.what: The calendar breaks. Ch2 is already the morning of the 26th ('Two nights. Now one had gone'), yet ch3, ch4 (second half) and ch5 each open again on the morning of the 26th, and ch6-7 are the 26th too. Five chapters replay the same day
issues.quote: The morning of the twenty sixth came in with heat already sitting on the roofs.

issues.what: Every chapter from 2 to 7 plans the rescue for 'tomorrow night', which falls after the 9 a.m. deadline on the 27th. The brief's premise (get him out before the guns fire) is dropped: the rescue in ch8 happens after the bombardment, so the ticking clock never matters
issues.quote: Tonight I will take my telescope to the roof again. You will come. We will watch the ships

issues.what: The brief's planned-moment text is pasted into the prose word for word, and a dialogue line reads the brief aloud
issues.quote: A plan with a skiff, a borrowed uniform and a flute tune only the siblings know. We made it

issues.what: The palace-courtyard visit happens four times (ch2, ch3, ch7, ch8) with the same beats each time: talk past the guard, hand out caps, straighten his cap, whisper the plan, he refuses. Ch8 even says 'It was easier the second time'
issues.quote: She talked her way into the palace courtyard with a basket of caps and found her brother proud

issues.what: The key backstory is told three incompatible ways. Ch1: she mentioned the pay two evenings earlier over rice and fried shark, two dollars a month, and he was mending sacks that morning. Ch2: over beans, three dollars. Ch6: at noon on the 25th, three rupees, and he took his father's rifle from under the bed. Ch8: he dropped a rice sack and ran after the crier
issues.quote: Three rupees and rice. I said it to fill silence.

issues.what: The flute and tune keep changing. Father cut the flute and whistled the tune (ch1); Khamis carved it from mangrove (ch6); the tune is Mama's supper call (ch5) or her pea-shelling song (ch6-8), learned 'last year'; it is 'four up, three down' (seven notes) or four notes; the cracked flute is a spare left at home (ch3) and also the one at his belt (ch6)
issues.quote: four notes her mother used to call them to supper when they played too far down the alley

issues.what: The borrowed uniform changes. Ch3: nephew Tomas's askari kanzu with red sash, and Tomas ran off to Mombasa. Ch5-8: Tomas is in town, works for customs, and lends a white suit for a goat
issues.quote: He has a white suit the English gave him for parade.

issues.what: History: at noon on 25 August the ships in harbour were Philomel, Thrush and Sparrow. St George (with Rawson) and Racoon arrived on the 26th, and the 9 a.m. ultimatum was issued on the 26th, not on the evening of the 25th. Five British ships fired on the 27th, not three
issues.quote: "St. George," he said, as if naming bulls. "Philomel. Sparrow."

issues.what: Khamis swears his oath with 'Juma and Fereji', but his friends are Saidi and Fadil and Juma is the old gate guard. The palace is 'Khalid Sayyid' here and 'Seyyid Khalid' elsewhere
issues.quote: With my friends. Juma and Fereji. We swore on the Book.

issues.what: Daudi leaves with the flute in his shirt, but at dawn it lies on the mat 'where Daudi had left it in the night'. Zuhura also sleeps at the studio, after ch1 worried that climbing to a man's roof would start talk
issues.quote: On the mat beside Zuhura, where Daudi had left it in the night, lay Khamis's small wooden flute.

issues.what: Repeated set pieces: the telescope on the roof, the guns swinging shoreward, and 'They mean it' / 'They always mean it' appear in ch1, 2, 4, 5 and 7. There are also small slips: 'A officer', 'the shadows shortened' in late afternoon, and a 'forward turret' on ships that had no turrets
issues.quote: "They mean it," she whispered. "They always mean it," Aurelio said.

issues.what: The brief asks for slavery to be handled honestly. The story's only mention is a passing 'slave market corner' (slavery was still legal in Zanzibar in 1896)
issues.quote: The sugar shop near the slave market corner was narrow and dark

fix: Regenerate with a single timeline. Ch1 = 25th, ships Philomel, Thrush and Sparrow, with the ultimatum only a rumour. Ch2-4 = 26th: St George and Racoon arrive and the ultimatum is formally issued. Ch5-7 = the last night, 26th to 27th, with the rescue attempt before dawn. Ch8 = 9:02-9:40 on the 27th and the aftermath. One palace visit, one account of the pay remark (she hides it), one flute and one tune, one uniform. Don't paste brief text.
praise: Chapter 1 is strong. Stone Town at noon, the fishbone of guilt, Khamis grinning through the gate, and Aurelio's 'Glass hates cannon' set up a story the later chapters lose.

issues.what: Safety: a child looks straight at the sun to read the dance, which is unsafe to imitate
issues.quote: Wumpini looked at the sun. She looked at her arrow.

issues.what: Fact precision: the bee waggles DURING the straight run, then loops back. The text reads as walk straight, then wiggle
issues.quote: She walked straight, wiggled, turned, came back, wiggled again.

issues.what: The planned smoke moment doesn't say what smoke does (it calms bees). 'The water pot flowers' is an odd phrase
issues.quote: Maybe the water pot flowers. Maybe the garden.

praise: Every bee fact is true and shown through what Wumpini draws: the angle from vertical means the angle from the sun, a longer waggle means farther, and a round dance means close. The race turns the science into the plot.

issues.what: Two hundred orbits is about two weeks, but the brief and the scene have her weak after months in orbit
issues.quote: I took it up. Two hundred orbits.

issues.what: Ages don't add up. Both are 43 and it has been twenty years, so Tuyen left at 23, not 18
issues.quote: You were eighteen. I was angry you wanted more.

issues.what: Tuyen's skin is 'cool from the capsule', but the capsule is still giving off heat and smells of hot wiring
issues.quote: Her skin was cool from the capsule

issues.what: The nephew vanishes while the two women have their private talk on a small boat. 'meters' clashes with the title's 'Kilometres'

praise: It is restrained and exact. The note under the biscuit tin, the fish that made two thousand orbits, and a touch that 'held twenty years' carry the feeling without melodrama.
